title: Summarize Anything, Your Way
problem: A plain 'summarize this' often comes back the wrong length, misses the part you actually cared about, or reads like a book report — because the model was never told what the summary is FOR, only what text to shrink.

workflow.detail: Say what you'll use the summary for — deciding something, skimming before a meeting, sharing with someone else. This changes what belongs in it more than the source text does.
Give a word count or number of bullets, not 'make it short' — a concrete number gets a far more consistent result.
If there's a tradeoff (numbers over narrative, decisions over discussion), say so explicitly.
Don't rely on the model to fetch or remember a document or link — paste the real content so it can't guess or hallucinate what's in it.
If the summary is missing something you needed, ask 'also pull out X' rather than rewriting the whole prompt.

variables.name: PURPOSE
variables.label: Purpose
variables.placeholder: e.g. Deciding whether to attend this event

variables.name: PRIORITY
variables.label: Prioritize
variables.placeholder: e.g. Dates, cost, and any action I need to take

variables.name: TEXT
variables.label: Text to summarize
variables.placeholder: Paste the actual email, article, or document text here...

exampleOutput:
- Event is Saturday, March 14, 6–9pm, downtown venue.
- Tickets are $45 until March 1, then $60.
- Action needed: RSVP by Feb 28 to get the early rate.
tips: Always paste the actual text rather than a link — most models can't reliably browse, and will otherwise guess at or invent the content.
'3 bullet points' gets a more consistent result than 'keep it short' — vague length requests produce inconsistent results across runs.
For very long documents, summarize in sections and then ask for a summary-of-summaries — a single giant paste can cause a model to skim the middle.
If you're going to make a decision based on the summary, skim the original source's key section yourself too — a summary trades detail for speed, which is sometimes the wrong trade.
